evidence.graph: home-sync node home.sync.homeness: the same four through the real CLI, asserted on exit code AND on nothing having been created
evidence.mutation: deleted the NotAHomeException.require call in HomeSync.run (1 occurrence, counted first) and both in HomeCloseOut.inspect (2 occurrences, both mutated); the named unit test failed with "it did NOT refuse, which is the defect"; reverted and verified with shasum -a 256 -c
evidence.unit: HomeSyncTest "close-out refuses a path that is not a home rather than clearing it" -- the worktree directory, a nonexistent path, a regular file, and the --into end, each asserted on the exception TYPE and on the real home being untouched

ticket.not_fixed_here: `home describe`, `home drift` and `home policy` also answer for arbitrary paths, and each calls store.init(), which lays out a home wherever it is pointed. Left alone on purpose and reported instead: `home policy frozen --home <a home being created>` is a real gesture, and none of the three claims anything about content or authorises a teardown. A command that says "there is nothing here to lose" is a different class of defect from one that leaves an empty directory tree at a mistyped path.
ticket.objective: `home close-out --home <the worktree DIRECTORY>` -- rather than <worktree>/.skill-manager -- exited 0 with "safe": true, "blockers": [], and printed the check mark line naming the directory that held the only copy of the agent's edit. So did a --home that did not exist at all. The gate FAILED OPEN, and the mistake is maximally likely: <worktree> is exactly the argument `git worktree remove` takes. Mechanism: nothing validated home-ness. HomeSync.unitsToVisit returns the union of both sides, a non-home yields zero units, every unit becomes REMOVED_UPSTREAM, and HomeCloseOut.remedyFor maps REMOVED_UPSTREAM to no blocker. Same hole on the sync side: `home sync --from <a nonexistent path>` printed "reconciled" with all-zero counts, exit 0, and created the destination's layout on the way; --from <a regular file> behaved identically.
ticket.resolution: NotAHomeException.require refuses before anything is read or written, for `home sync --from`, `home close-out --home` and `home close-out --into`. Home-ness is decided by LaunchEnv.looksLikeStoreRoot, made public rather than re-spelled: it already encoded the test for the PATH sanitizer, and three spellings of "is this a home" would eventually disagree about exactly the homes where it matters. Exit code 2, distinct from 0 (reconciled / safe), 1 (this home still holds work) and 9 (refused by policy); --json callers get {"error":"not_a_home", "safe":false, "clean":false} rather than a stack trace, so a script cannot read the refusal as approval. A sync DESTINATION is deliberately not validated: creating a tier by reconciling into it is the operation this epic exists for.
